 THIS PETITION IS COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent/State and perused the material on record.
2. Petitioner, arraigned as accused No.2 in Crime No.8/2023 of Hassan Extension Police Station,
registered for offences punishable under Sections 408, 409, 420 of IPC has preferred this petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail.
3. The complainant is working as Senior Manager of one CMS Company.

The complaint averments are that the said company is having several private sector banks like Axis bank, ICICI, HDFC etc as customers and it is responsible for the collection of cash and its deposit through out Karnataka.
The company has about 20,000/- employees and provides about 3,000 cash pick up points.

It is alleged that accused No.1, working as executive NC: 2023:KHC:21214 operation since 2019 entrusted with the duty to collect money from the customers, who are tie up with the complainant's company and then to deposit the same in ICICI Bank, Santhepete Circle, B.M.Road, Hassan, in collusion with accused No.2 i.e., the petitioner herein working as a Manager at Hassan Branch, collected money from different customers but failed to deposit it to the bank and thereby misappropriated to the tune of Rs.26,80,709/-.
4. As per the complaint averments, the petitioner is working as Manager of the company at Hassan Branch.

It is stated that on being informed by the Head office in Mumbai, about the misappropriation, complainant enquired with the petitioner herein, who told that the amount was collected by accused No.1, but failed to deposit to the bank.

5. It is contended by the learned counsel for petitioner that the main allegations are against accused No.1 and this petitioner has infact informed the NC: 2023:KHC:21214 complainant about the non deposit of the amount by the said accused.
He submits that accused No.1 has been enlarged on bail by this Court and the petitioner is ready and willing to cooperate with the investigation of the case.

6. The learned High Court Government Pleader submits that the investigation is pending and in the event of grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner, he may not cooperate with the investigation and Harish Kumar vs The State Of Karnataka By on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159739350/
2 he may destroy evidence.

sentences.text: It is alleged that from 26.12.2022 to 04.01.2023, the amount collected from Reliance Retail and Instacot Organization was not deposited.
The allegations against the petitioner is that he has colluded with accused No.1 and misappropriated the said amount.

At this stage there is no sufficient material to show that the petitioner has misappropriated the amount to the tune of Rs.26,80,709/-
as alleged in the complaint.
The petitioner has undertaken to cooperate with the investigation of the case.
Accused No.1 has been granted bail in Criminal NC: 2023:KHC:21214 Petition No.2265/2023 vide order dated 13.06.2023.
Hence by imposing suitable conditions, the relief sought by the petitioner can be granted.

Accordingly the following:
ORDER i. The petition is allowed.
ii. In the event of arrest of the petitioner in Crime No.8/2023 of Hassan Extn. Police Station he shall be released, subject to following conditions:
i. Petitioner shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- [Rupees Two Lakhs only] with one surety for the likesum.
 ii. Petitioner shall cooperate with the  investigation and he shall not  tamper with the prosecution  evidence/witnesses in any  manner.
Petitioner shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court regarding change in the address, if any.
iv. Petitioner shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.

Sd/-
